text:
marco: heads-up — new int4 canary (kestrel-mini-int4) shows funcall parse anomalies. rate ~6.3% on short chat completions. root cause looks like escape-seq fragmentation across chunk boundaries (backslash at end of chunk).

june: can you paste an example bytestring?

marco: sample (escaped for readability): ```{\"action\":\"emit\",\"payload\":\"Path: C:\\\\Users\\\\alice\\\\notes.txt\\\"}\n``` Here the model emitted a trailing backslash inside the string and the kernel flush split it so consumer sees `...\\\\notes.txt\\` then newline. strict JSON parse fails with `Trailing \` error.

oliver: ah, so the chunk boundary left a lone backslash which makes the decoder think the string didn't finish. this is distinct from BOM/null we saw — it's about escape bytes split.

priyanka: telemetry: query `parse_fail_rate by model,seq_len,reason` shows majority labeled `invalid_escape` and concentrated at seq_len <80 and batch_size=1. fp16 baseline negligible. uploaded 30 raw traces to s3://canary/escapefrag/1723456789.

canary-bot: deploy kestrel-mini-int4 @ 1723456000 -> hostset alpha. last 30m: 44 successes / 3 failures. failing ids: cnry-1723456601, cnry-1723456699, cnry-1723457010.

ken: mitigation proposal: on strict parse error inspect last 8 bytes of the payload; if it ends with an odd number of backslashes and the rest of the JSON decodes after removing trailing backslashes, attempt a rescue that reattaches the missing escape by appending a placeholder escape target (e.g., `\\\"` -> `\\\"PLACEHOLDER\\\"`) then validate schema and run golden-check. Tag telemetry `rescue=escape_repair`.

marta: i worry about mutating string contents. adding placeholder text could alter semantics. alternative: request a retry to the model with same prompt and short max_tokens to let it finish the escape, up to retry budget. if retry succeeds, prefer that over mutation.

june: agreement: try retry-first policy: 1) on invalid_escape attempt a fast single retry (budgeted) 2) if retry fails and payload ends with backslash run a conservative sanitizer that removes trailing backslashes (not adding placeholders) then strict-parse and tag `rescue=escape_strip`. Record diff and compare to golden set.

oliver: implementation note: the strip must only touch trailing backslashes that are outside quoted escape sequences (i.e., trailing run of `\\+` at EOF). safe to strip when not inside an open string? need a small UTF-8 aware byte scanner to determine inside_string state.

priyanka: i ran a local experiment: retry succeeded 58% of the time for these cases, and `escape_strip` recovered another 27%. overall would cut user-facing failures ~85% while we fix kernel.

marta: kernel action: quant team to avoid splitting `\\` tokens across flush boundaries. file QNT-834; suggested approach: if last byte of chunk == `\\` then delay flush one token or emit an explicit continuation marker byte outside JSON stream. quant to investigate this week.

ken: monitoring: add `escape_repair_rate` and `escape_retry_success` series to dashboard, alert if repair_rate >3% for 30m. also run golden-funcall check comparing sanitized/retried outputs to ground truth for 2k samples; if mismatch >0.3% pause auto-rescue.

marco: action items: june to implement retry-first rescue flow + telemetry (PR by EOD), oliver to add byte-scanner util and unit tests, marta to coordinate QNT-834 with quant, ken to add alerts. i'll run a 12h soft canary with rescue opt-in on 10% hosts and report. :eyes:

june: pushing a small harness that reproduces the split locally and a snippet for the retry path. will link in PR.

marco: thanks all — ping me for s3 access. we'll use conservative defaults until kernel fix lands. :thumbsup:
